rv.q: Magic Mike Live is entertaining, funny and, yes, very horny.
It's probably best experienced with a group of friends — and after a few drinks.
Magic Mike Live delivers exactly what it promises.
Magic Mike’s London outing doesn’t feel remotely like it’s been written for a woke London audience, especially with jokes as in-your-face as those bulges.
It is the weirdest, most monetised, almost sexual experience of my life.
Initially, at least, the show is so determined to prove its woke credentials, it drags out the set-up for too long: there’s too much telling and not enough showing, for want of a better phrase.
It’s deeply odd, swinging between silly and unthreatening, with the kind of cautious dancing you might do with an elderly aunt at a wedding and full-on, oily lap-dances.
The evening of talent, dancing, and, honestly, joy and empowerment taking place at the Hippodrome Casino is a feat of live entertainment.
Magic Mike won't stretch your mind. It won't melt your heart. But it might just make you cackle with laughter and there's abs-olutely nothing wrong with that.
Let go of every expectation you have about a show called Magic Mike Live
Soaked with sex, riddled with romance and awash with washboard abs, the lads say they hope this production will appeal to all women.

‘ARE YOU ready to get more suspect meat than a late-night kebab?’ is the clarion call that comes (sorry) at the start of Magic Mike Live. ‘Whoooooooo!’ came (again, sorry) the inevitable response from a tanked-up, oestrogen-rich Tuesday night crowd, who were about to witness a Loose Woman’s wet dream. Theatre, this ain’t.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this high-energy spectacle: some praise the impressive dancing and fun, empowering atmosphere, while others dismiss it as shallow entertainment that prioritizes spectacle over substance.
